A search for Bartholomew Flynn as a possible brother of Patrick Flynn turned up nothing at all. Nine different queries were run against FamilySearch's historical records — starting with Pennsylvania, then broadening to all of the United States, then to Ireland, then dropping all location filters entirely, and trying spelling variants (Flinn, Fl*nn), name wildcards (Barth*, Bat*), and even anchoring the search on the known father Thomas Flynn rather than on Bartholomew's own name. This does not prove Bartholomew Flynn never existed. It means he is not currently indexed on FamilySearch under any of the spellings and filters tried. Records that are actually absent from the index entirely — not just hard to spell — are a known gap in FamilySearch's coverage, especially for Irish-born immigrants in mid-19th-century Pennsylvania.

**Next steps:** If corroborating a Bartholomew Flynn is important to the parentage question, consider:
- Searching Ancestry and other repositories that index the same record sets differently
- Exploring unindexed Pennsylvania county records and Irish Catholic parish registers through image browsing
- Trying a full-text search approach for mentions of Bartholomew as a non-principal (witness, heir, neighbor)

Nine searches logged as log_005 through log_013. No plan item to update (ad-hoc search).

---

A search for Bartholomew Flynn as a possible brother of Patrick Flynn turned up nothing at all. Nine different queries were run against FamilySearch's historical records — starting with Pennsylvania, then broadening to all of the United States, then to Ireland, then dropping all location filters entirely, and trying spelling variants (Flinn, Fl*nn), name wildcards (Barth*, Bat*), and even anchoring the search on the known father Thomas Flynn rather than on Bartholomew's own name. Every single search returned zero results.

This does not prove Bartholomew Flynn never existed. It means he is not currently indexed on FamilySearch under any of the spellings and filters tried. He may appear in records that were filmed but never indexed (browse-only image volumes, such as undigitized Pennsylvania county registers or Irish Catholic parish books), or he may have died in Ireland before emigrating, or the name may have been so severely corrupted in an index that no variation reached it. Records that are actually absent from the index entirely — not just hard to spell — are a known gap in FamilySearch's coverage, especially for Irish-born immigrants in mid-19th-century Pennsylvania.

The next step, if corroborating a Bartholomew Flynn is important to the parentage question, would be to search Ancestry and other repositories that index the same record sets differently, or to explore unindexed Pennsylvania county records and Irish Catholic parish registers through image browsing or a full-text search approach.
